specDepartures.spec: The spec names the listener's own code and the corrected text as the change, and the production record as moving the in-cluster listener's image pin in theorem-labs/agent-infra; it leaves to the plan which input tells a listener whether its grant allows every notification topic.
specDepartures.plan: The input is an opt-in, ENVOY_SUBSCRIBE_ALL_TOPICS=1, off by default. The plan also changes the envoy-infra plugin (core.ListenerConfig.SubscribeAllTopics and an optional subscribeAllTopics input on host:Listener and aws:WebhookListener, plus envoy-infra render's flag), sets it in both compose files, and adds it to the in-cluster listener's environment in the same agent-infra change that moves the pin.
specDepartures.evidence: Nothing a listener reads tells ListenerPermissions (hub, Dispatch: infra/core/permissions.go:50-69,108-125) from HostPermissions (:150-156); NATS reports no grant and a probing subscribe is a refusal the live grant tests fail on; the hub cannot opt out without a cloud-config re-render that replaces its VM; the component-rendered and hand-written environments (infra/host/listener.go:106, infra/aws/rendering/listener.go:120, agent-infra envoy-cluster/listener.go:117-123) have no other way to set it. Every existing rendering, the hub's and Dispatch's included, stays byte-identical.

outcome.scope: Adds the envoy-infra plugin's ListenerConfig field and optional subscribeAllTopics inputs on host:Listener and aws:WebhookListener, the two compose files, and one environment variable in the agent-infra change the production record already needs.

specDepartures.spec: The spec's address rule: a session on the listener's own machine is reached at ENVOY_HOST_BRIDGE wherever one is configured; otherwise at the host the registration records; else host.docker.internal for its own machine and the machine's name for another, so any listener prompts a session on a pod or machine beside it.
specDepartures.plan: Only the owner of a serving-port session delivers to it (the listener its stored subscription names, else the one it registered through); any other listener refuses with session.ErrWrongMachine and requests nothing. The owner uses its bridge only for a session on its own machine: the entry names the owner or no listener, or the recorded host equals the owner's ENVOY_MACHINE_ID (case-insensitive); otherwise the recorded host, else host.docker.internal for its own registration, else the registering listener's machine id.
specDepartures.evidence: Every listener reads each inbox message from its own durable, so under the spec's rule two listeners that could reach a session each delivered it (tester: two prompts per inbox message at d73383ee). The architect chose owner-only delivery (round 3), the stored subscription as owner (round 4), the bridge limit (dispatch://INFRA-122/comment/e71c1010-473a-4c71-87b1-9f15c186f4eb) and the stayed-local clause (decision B, 2026-10-26 04:38Z); review round 3 measured a lost message when a bridged owner dialled its own bridge for a session on another machine.

outcome.scope: The address rule is built per owner: a non-owning listener never prompts a serving-port session, and the bridge applies only to a session on the owner's machine. Acceptance line 5 holds through the owner (the session is reached at its recorded host by the listener that owns it), not through any listener.
acceptance: 5. A session is reached by the address rule above, so a listener prompts a session on a pod beside it: reached by its owning listener, under the owner and bridge rule of decision 4.
